traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and requirements from docs/stories/022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE.story.md are implemented and verified:
- **Before/After/Mixed JSDoc Tags**: Tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts cover traceability annotations before other tags, after them, and interspersed with @param/@returns. All are in the `valid` set and pass, confirming REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE. - **Proper Termination & Boundary Detection**: The helper isNonTraceabilityJSDocTagLine treats any line starting with `@` (except @story/@req/@supports) as a JSDoc boundary. processCommentLine finalizes any pending @story/@req when such a line is seen, preventing concatenation across tags and satisfying REQ-ANNOTATION-TERMINATION and REQ-JSDOC-BOUNDARY-DETECTION. - **Continuation Logic & Multiline Values**: Continuation of a pending annotation only occurs on non-empty, non-tag lines; multi-line @story examples immediately followed by @param/@returns are tested and pass, fulfilling REQ-CONTINUATION-LOGIC and REQ-PRESERVE-MULTILINE. - **No False Positives / Clear Errors**: The specific bug scenario from the story (an @req followed by @param/@returns) is now a `valid` test case and passes, confirming JSDoc tags no longer pollute the requirement ID (REQ-NO-FALSE-POSITIVES). Existing invalid cases for genuinely malformed annotations continue to produce clear, specific error messages; the full Jest suite passes, indicating backward compatibility. - **Documentation**: docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md has an explicit “JSDoc coexistence” section with behavior description and a full example using this story’s path, meeting the documentation acceptance criterion.
With implementation, tests, and documentation aligned and all Jest suites passing, Story 022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE is fully implemented and verified.
